hero.alt: A Jeffy blast lights a Bulldog among healthy synthesized trees on Greenhaven in Nanolathe’s Modern GPU renderer.
hero.caption: A staged battle on Greenhaven, rendered in Nanolathe.

sections.title: Zoom out to plan a battle
sections.how: The camera runs from a 2× close-up to a view of the whole map. When units get too small to make out, team-colored icons show their type and position.
sections.capture: Twenty-six engine captures cover the camera’s zoom range. The slider starts at 1×, reaches 2× detail and pulls back to the camera’s whole-map minimum, 0.078125×. Thirty-nine staged units use settled, activated COB poses. The second solar was moved onto clear ground and a metal extractor occupies the deposit. Unit placements stay fixed; the camera pans at wide scales and fog is omitted. Each stop is native 960 × 640; no image is enlarged to simulate camera zoom.

zoomViewer.alt: Greenhaven outpost at the engine’s original 1× camera scale, with the metal extractor on its deposit.
zoomViewer.caption: Greenhaven outpost with 39 staged units. Each zoom level is a separate engine capture.

sections.title: More detail from the original tiles
sections.how: The native engine generates larger terrain tiles by matching small patches of TA’s original artwork. A 32 × 32 tile becomes 64 × 64, and tree sprites get the same 2× treatment. The result is cached locally, so it can be reused next time you play.
sections.look: The grass and leaves show the difference at this distance. Both views use the same 2× camera.
sections.capture: A close Greenhaven view is rendered twice through Modern GPU, using original artwork and then real synthesized terrain and foliage. Both captures share the same camera and committed state. Healthy native leaf sprites are used; authored dead stumps are cleared in this staged display. Native 480 × 320 captures show a smaller area at the same 2× camera. Shadow or missing variants keep the engine’s normal fallback.
sections.caption: Original and synthesized terrain and trees on Greenhaven, at the same zoom.
sections.altBefore: Original grass and healthy leaf trees at the same close Greenhaven camera
sections.altAfter: The same Greenhaven grass and trees with real 2× synthesized terrain and foliage

sections.title: Explosions light nearby units
sections.how: An explosion lights the ground and nearby models as well as drawing its own sprite. Bright effects also get a soft glow. This scene compares the full Classic and Modern renderers.
sections.look: The armor on the Bulldog beside the exploding Jeffy shows the extra lighting clearly.
sections.capture: A Jeffy self-destructs beside a Bulldog among healthy Greenhaven trees. Classic CPU and Modern GPU share the same committed tick 132 and 2× camera. Modern uses real 2× synthesized terrain and foliage, with default anti-aliasing, lighting and glow at native strengths. The clearing removes burn successors and authored dead stumps; the surrounding trees remain healthy. Full renderer comparison, native 960 × 640. The accompanying video is 3 seconds at 30 FPS.
sections.caption: The same Jeffy explosion in Classic and Modern, with a Bulldog beside it.
sections.altBefore: A Jeffy explosion beside a Bulldog in Nanolathe’s Classic CPU renderer
sections.altAfter: The same explosion and Bulldog in the Modern GPU renderer with synthesized terrain, lighting and glow

extraMotion.label: Matched Classic and Modern engine footage of a Jeffy explosion beside a Bulldog
extraMotion.caption: The same staged explosion in both renderers. Switching views keeps the current playback position.

sections.title: Water
sections.how: The modern renderer adds moving water, shoreline foam, reflections and underwater refraction. This interactive browser study uses the engine’s water equations with original transport and submarine models on Gods of War terrain.
sections.look: Pause the water and toggle the effects separately. The submarine shows refraction; the transport’s crane is visible in the reflection.
sections.capture: This live WebGL water study uses frozen, activated transport and submarine poses exported at committed tick 31 from engine 617540c5. Original palette textures, the native terrain view and the engine’s projected shoreline mask are retained. Water field, surface shading, damp shoreline, foam, refraction and reflection ripple/tint/opacity arithmetic are adapted at native strengths. The sampled wind direction and tidal rate remain fixed. WebGL triangle/depth rasterization, texture filtering, and reflected-mesh occlusion differ from the native height-key screen-space resolve. It does not simulate units, COB wakes, shadow passes or gameplay. The native Metal engine recording below includes moving units, real wakes and evolving wind. The native video is 6 seconds at 30 FPS.

motion.label: A transport reflects on Gods of War water alongside a refracted submarine and shoreline foam
motion.caption: Native engine footage on Gods of War, with moving units and their wakes.

sections.title: Metal and painted surfaces
sections.how: Metal textures catch broad highlights and directional glints, while painted panels have a softer finish. The model keeps its original colors and panel seams.
sections.look: Rotate the unit or orbit the light to see the highlights move. Hold the angle still to compare with the finish turned off.
sections.capture: This ARM mobile Annihilator model and its texture atlas were exported from engine 801c8b2. WebGL adapts the engine’s metal/paint finish and glint arithmetic; rotation, tilt and an optional light orbit are study controls. Its projection, depth testing, anti-aliasing and floor shadow differ from the game renderer. It is a material study, not a playable unit. The native Metal engine comparison below was captured at 279f7af1.

motion.label: The original ARM mobile Annihilator rotates in the native engine to show materials and glints
motion.caption: The original ARM mobile Annihilator, with the surface finish off and on in the native engine.

sections.title: Smoother unit edges
sections.how: Modern anti-aliasing draws models at twice the resolution in each direction, then combines four samples per output pixel. It works on mobile units and their moving parts as well as buildings.
sections.look: Compare the gun barrels and diagonal armor across these nine models. Both renderer paths have anti-aliasing enabled; Modern extends it to mobile units.
sections.capture: Bulldog, Maverick, Zeus, Reaper, Annihilator, Stumpy, Merl, Goliath and a construction Kbot share committed poses and the 2× camera. Both renderer paths have anti-aliasing enabled: Classic retains structure coverage, while Modern extends it to mobile units. Vegetation is cleared from the tableau so it does not hide the models. Whole renderer paths, native 960 × 640.
sections.caption: The same unit lineup in Classic and Modern, with anti-aliasing enabled in both.
sections.altBefore: An original model lineup showing mobile units and a building in Nanolathe’s Classic CPU renderer
sections.altAfter: The same original models and camera with full-unit anti-aliasing in Nanolathe’s Modern GPU renderer

sections.title: Heat above burning trees
sections.how: Burning vegetation distorts the view behind the rising heat. Turning shimmer off leaves the original flame and smoke sprites in place.
sections.look: Watch the grass just above the three burning palms. You can pause the clip and toggle shimmer on the same frame.
sections.capture: Three original architree01 palms are placed and ignited through the real feature service. Session.Step advances their flames, smoke and burning lifecycle. Matched Modern GPU views toggle only FireShimmer. The 2× camera and native effect strength remain fixed; no image resampling or retiming is used. Captured at 480 × 320, 5 seconds at 30 FPS.

motion.label: Heat distortion above three burning palms
motion.caption: Burning palms on Great Divide, with heat shimmer off and on.

sections.title: Wrecks cool after a kill
sections.how: Fresh wrecks glow and distort the air, then return to their normal textures as they cool. This follows the wreck’s age in the engine.
sections.look: The Stumpy is destroyed one second into the clip. Let it play to the end to see the glow and shimmer fade.
sections.capture: A Stumpy takes ordinary nonlethal damage during warmup, then an ordinary lethal damage packet one second into the clip. Its COB Killed result places the real corpse at tick 120. Paired Modern views toggle WreckGlow and WreckShimmer, preserving the explosion, materials and every other effect. The 13-second clip includes cooling and shimmer expiry; native 480 × 320 at the 2× camera. The video runs at 30 FPS.

motion.label: A Stumpy is destroyed and its wreck cools
motion.caption: A Stumpy on Great Divide, from destruction through cooling.

sections.title: Shadows soften with altitude
sections.how: An aircraft’s shadow spreads out as its height above the ground increases. The renderer softens the original silhouette while keeping narrow shapes, such as wings, connected.
sections.look: These Hurricanes are fixed at two different heights. Compare the tighter shadow on the left with the softer one on the right.
sections.capture: Two original CORE Hurricane bombers are staged at 60 and 180 world units above Greenhaven’s ground. Their original activated COB poses, heights, heading and 2× camera stay fixed. The actual Metal renderer executes the same cloned drawlist with only SoftShadows off and on; ShadowSoftness remains 100%. The on/off/on replay restores identical pixels, and the committed publication remains unchanged. Vegetation is omitted from this presentation fixture to keep both shadows visible. This is a frozen altitude study, not simulated flight. Native 960 × 640; no resampling or retouching.
sections.caption: Two Hurricanes over Greenhaven, fixed at different heights. The higher one is on the right.
sections.altBefore: Two CORE Hurricane bombers at different heights with ordinary silhouette shadows on Greenhaven
sections.altAfter: The same two bombers and camera with the modern altitude-dependent soft aircraft shadows

overview.title: Tracks and scorch marks
overview.text: Units leave footprints and tank tracks. Explosions leave scorch marks that fade over time.

overview.title: Movement between ticks
overview.text: Presentation interpolation smooths movement between simulation ticks without changing the simulation itself.

overview.title: Blast rings and glow settings
overview.text: Refractive rings distort the scene around a blast. Weapons, explosions and construction have separate glow-strength settings.
